questions.question: 1. Why does a food sample lose or gain weight when placed in a desiccator with controlled relative humidity?

answers.b: Due to equilibrium moisture exchange with the environment

questions.question: 2. In the experiment, which sample is likely to exhibit the highest microbial growth?

answers.a: The sample in the 0% sulfuric acid solution
answers.b: The sample in the 70% sulfuric acid solution
answers.c: The sample in an intermediate concentration (e.g., 50%)
answers.d: The sample in the 10% sulfuric acid solution

questions.question: 3. What can be inferred if the bread sample in a particular desiccator shows minimal weight change over 9 days?

answers.a: The sample is resistant to microbial growth
answers.b: The relative humidity of the desiccator matches the sample's equilibrium moisture content
answers.c: The sample absorbed all the available water
answers.d: The sulfuric acid concentration was incorrect

questions.question: 4. What is the primary cause of microbial growth in high-moisture environments?

answers.b: High relative humidity supporting water activity

questions.question: 5. How does this experiment help in food preservation techniques?

answers.a: By identifying optimal storage conditions to prevent spoilage
answers.b: By determining the nutrient content of food samples
answers.c: By enhancing the flavor of food through humidity control
answers.d: By eliminating all microbes from food samples
